balance_review.finding: CPU extensions fell from a mean of 130.333 to 99.667; free-agent signings increased. Mean FA annual pay stayed close and no long-contract pileup appeared.
balance_review.diagnosis: Targeted extension tracing found refusals on strongly backloaded packages and offers below adjusted expectations. These are reasons to review behavior, not to force players to sign.
balance_review.caveat: Stable profiles intentionally stop consuming simulation RNG, so identical seeds no longer imply identical downstream draws. Counts do not isolate a single coefficient.
balance_review.recommendation: Bounded CPU counter handling is implemented and validated. No acceptance quota or relaxation of firm refusals. Ready for integration review; retain forecast and long-run limitations.

individual_refusal_audit.decision: HOLD broad release: CPU extension callers discard economic counters and never test affordable alternative payment schedules
individual_refusal_audit.scope: Three extension-stage runs of one saved league; seed 481 followed through all three FA rounds and market close
findings: A countered player is not necessarily making a firm refusal to negotiate or electing free agency. Keep those policies distinct.
CPU ai_round and in_season_round only handle accepted extension results; economic counters are discarded.
At unchanged annual pay, years and signing bonus, 62 rejected offers became acceptable and passed current/future cap guards when salary was distributed evenly.
EXT.extend returns only annual ask and years for counters, omitting the payment structure and bonus underpinning the reference value.
No moving quote was observed between initial CPU pricing and the actual player assessment in these attempts.
individual_refusal_audit.recommended_fix: Return a complete economic counter, and let the CPU consider a small set of payment schedules within its valuation, cap and commitment limits before choosing to walk away. Preserve all hard refusals and do not force an acceptance quota.
